files.why: Add invoice-level discount to the entity (e.g. discountCode + discountMinor) on Invoice, and mirror the discounted total in InvoiceSummary — pure, framework-free state the total math reads.
Fold the discount into invoiceTotalMinor (and summarize) so 'reduces the total' is a pure, tested domain rule, not UI subtraction.
Add canApplyDiscount gating (e.g. not on paid/void), mirroring canVoid/canEditLines — the business rule for when a code may be applied.
Extend invoiceDtoSchema with the server's discount fields (code string + decimal-string amount) so validated server shapes carry the applied discount.
Map discount DTO fields to/from core (decimal string ↔ minor units) in toInvoice/toInvoiceDto, keeping DTO shapes out of core.
Add applyDiscountCode(id, code) → PATCH endpoint → validated Invoice, mirroring voidInvoice; the server owns code validity so this is the apply action.
Add an MSW handler for the apply-discount endpoint (valid vs invalid/expired code) plus discount fields on seed invoices so the flow runs against the mock API.
Expose an applyDiscount(code) action with pending/error state and recomputed totals, wiring the mutation into the detail view state.
Add the discount-code input + Apply button and a discount row in the totals <dl> (invoice-level discount belongs with Subtotal/Tax/Total, not in the lines table).
Cover discounted invoiceTotalMinor/summarize and the canApplyDiscount policy — the contract that a code reduces the total, tested purely.
Assert the discount fields round-trip through toInvoice/toInvoiceDto and stay schema-valid.

uncertain: Discount representation: I modeled an INVOICE-level discount (discountCode + resolved discountMinor from the server) because 'apply a code' is an action with server-side validation. The README's worked example instead adds a static per-line discountBps and says to extend InvoiceLinesTable.vue with a column. If the team means the README's model, the lines-table edit replaces my InvoiceDetailView totals-row edit and the mutation/apply-code plumbing largely disappears.

Whether the discount-code input is a new billing/ui/components/*.vue (its own valid/invalid/pending reason to change, per rules 6/7) or stays inline in InvoiceDetailView.vue. I kept it inline (single use, duplicate-before-promote), but a small ApplyDiscountForm.vue is defensible.

Placement of the apply-eligibility check: I put canApplyDiscount in core/policy.ts alongside canVoid, but it could instead be enforced only server-side (then policy.ts is untouched and the UI just reacts to the mutation's error).

index.ts is intentionally NOT modified: the discount is internal to billing and folds into the already-exported InvoiceSummary.totalMinor, so no new public export or cross-slice edge. Flagging in case a consumer needs to show discount separately.
questions: Is a discount code server-validated (code → amount/percent resolved by the API, which is what I assumed) or does the client hold a code catalog? This decides whether resolution logic lives in core/ or stays entirely in data/+server.
Is the discount a percentage (bps) or a fixed amount, and does it apply per-line or to the invoice subtotal/total? Affects the rules.ts math and rounding.
Does tax apply before or after the discount (discount the pre-tax subtotal vs the gross total)? This changes invoiceTotalMinor ordering and the tax figure shown.
One code per invoice or stackable codes? Determines whether the field is a single value or a collection.
Which invoice statuses accept a code (draft/issued only? never paid/void?), and can a customer remove a previously applied code?
What are the invalid-code UX states (unknown, expired, minimum-not-met) the view must render, and are their messages server- or client-provided?
